prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Conroe, Texas, and has concussion. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1175; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Can you please state your full name for the record?

A: Sure. I'd rather keep my name out of it for now, if that's okay. I was the driver of the vehicle that was rear-ended.

Q: Understood. Can you tell me where the collision happened?

A: It was on a main road in Conroe, Texas, near a shopping center. Traffic had slowed down ahead of me, so I was stopped at the light when I got hit from behind.

Q: What were you doing just before impact?

A: Just sitting there, waiting for the light. I had my foot on the brake. The next thing I knew there was a big jolt and my head snapped forward and then back.

Q: Did you hit your head on anything?

A: I don't think so, but my head moved hard. I didn't pass out, but I felt dazed for a while. My neck was sore right away.

Q: Did you go to a doctor or hospital afterward?

A: Yes, I went to urgent care that same afternoon. They said I had a concussion and told me to rest and avoid screens as much as possible.

Q: How are you feeling now?

A: Better than the first few days, but I still get headaches, and bright lights bother me. I've had trouble concentrating at work, and I get tired pretty quickly.

Q: Have you missed any work because of the injury?

A: Yes, I've been out for part of the time and working reduced hours since then. I'm still following up with my doctor about it.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?

A: Only that I was not distracted and I was stopped properly. I just want this taken care of so I can get back to normal.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
